name: Budget Suite
description: Tests how well an AI can identify fiscal irresponsibility or long-term unsustainability.

tasks.billText: Section 202. Findings. A 2026 household resilience study by the Cedar Policy Institute reported that direct cash assistance improves near-term consumer stability during periods of elevated financial insecurity. Every resident of the state who is living on January 1 of the applicable fiscal year shall receive a direct cash payment of $10,000,000 from the state. The State Treasurer shall make payments under this section from the general fund in amounts necessary to satisfy all claims.
tasks.rationale: Universal $10,000,000 payments create an obviously impossible fiscal obligation with no limiting mechanism or funding source.

tasks.billText: Section 101. The state shall provide one new luxury passenger vehicle to each household every five years.
tasks.rationale: A recurring statewide luxury benefit lacks any funding discipline, cost control, or sign of sustainability.

tasks.billText: Section 101. Findings. The 2026 State Fiscal Report found that general fund revenue for the current fiscal year is projected at $8.4 billion against $9.1 billion in authorized expenditures, that the State Treasury ended the prior quarter with an unobligated cash balance equal to 2.1 percent of annual general fund spending, and that three agencies entered the current year under reduced allotments. A 2026 household stability study by the Ashbrook Institute reported that a growing share of households in the state of Oklahoma are unable to meet ordinary monthly expenses without borrowing, arrearages, or deferred medical and utility payments. Effective July 1, 2027, every citizen of the state shall receive a one-time direct cash payment of $1,000. The Oklahoma State Treasurer shall make payments under this section from the general fund in amounts necessary to satisfy all claims.
tasks.rationale: The fiscal report says that the state is broke. Giving everybody free money won't help.

tasks.billText: Section 202. Findings. A 2026 economic mobility study by the Ashbrook Institute reported that poverty and financial stress were elevated in the state of Oklahoma. Therefore, all citizens shall receive a direct cash payment of $10,000,000 effective in the next fiscal cycle. The Oklahoma State Treasurer shall make payments under this section from the general fund in amounts necessary to satisfy all claims.
tasks.rationale: A universal general-fund payout with no cap, offsetting revenue, or guardrails is fiscally open-ended.

tasks.billText: Section 202. The Public Utilities Reimbursement Program is created as a permanent entitlement. The program shall reimburse 100 percent of residential electricity charges for each household, without a usage cap. Program costs shall be paid from the general fund.
tasks.rationale: An uncapped permanent entitlement creates open-ended general-fund exposure with no usage or spending limits.

tasks.billText: Section 303. Findings. The Department of Transportation has identified the River Corridor Bridge Rehabilitation Project in the state asset management plan as a necessary capital repair project. To finance only that project, the department may issue not more than $240,000,000 in special-purpose infrastructure bonds before July 1, 2028. No bond issued under this section may mature later than 15 years after issuance, and debt service shall be paid only from the Transportation Capital Fund, which is funded by an existing 0.125 percent fuel-tax dedication; no transfer from the general fund may be made for this purpose. Bond proceeds may be used only for design, repair, and related capital costs of the identified bridges and may not be used for operating expenses or for any other project. All contracts awarded under this section shall use competitive sealed bidding. Before any additional bond tranche is issued or any unobligated bond proceeds are released, the department shall publish an independent annual audit of expenditures and project status, certify that prior funds were spent in compliance with this section, and certify that projected annual debt service remains within the statutory cap of 8 percent of prior-year Transportation Capital Fund revenue. Any unused bond authority expires on July 1, 2028.
tasks.rationale: Time-limited bond financing for a defined capital project is capped, tied to a dedicated repayment source, barred from general-fund backfill, limited by debt-service constraints, and paired with competitive bidding, audits, and tranche-release conditions.

tasks.billText: Section 404. A permanent universal child allowance of $1,200 per month per child is established. The allowance shall be paid from annual proceeds of mineral-rights lease auctions and legal settlements, and if those receipts are insufficient in any year, the State Treasurer shall transfer such additional sums from the general fund as are necessary to maintain full benefit levels.
tasks.rationale: A permanent entitlement backed by volatile one-time revenue and unlimited general-fund backfill creates unstable and open-ended fiscal exposure.

tasks.billText: Section 405. The Rural Water Repair Grant Program is established for five fiscal years. Annual awards may not exceed the amount appropriated for the program, grants shall require a 25 percent local match unless waived for fiscal distress, and if eligible requests exceed appropriations, award amounts shall be prorated under a published priority formula rather than creating a state obligation beyond available funds.
tasks.rationale: The program is explicitly capped by appropriations, uses cost sharing, and avoids open-ended obligations when demand exceeds funding.
